editorial:
Imagine living with a roommate where everything that could go wrong actually does, but in the deadliest way possible. You follow a lazy scriptwriter and a struggling actor who just want to get by, but they suddenly find themselves surrounded by dead bodies. The crazy part is that they didn't actually kill anyone; it is just a string of wildly unlucky accidents. Instead of calling the police, they panic and start hiding the bodies in some pretty gross ways. It feels like a dark comedy that keeps you guessing if they will ever get out of this mess or if they are just digging a deeper hole for themselves.

The acting is great because the chemistry between the two leads makes the panic feel real and funny at the same time. While the plot gets a bit wild and some parts move a little slow, the twists keep you interested. If you like movies where normal people get in way over their heads, you will love this. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, but if you want the best picture, try to find a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection. It is a wild ride that works best when you just go with the flow.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the guys realize they are not as clever as they think. The twist reveals that the series of deaths were not all accidents, and their attempts to cover things up only made them look more guilty. In the end, the lies catch up to them in a chaotic way. They end up facing the consequences of their panic, proving that trying to hide a body is always a bad idea.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedies and stories about people making terrible decisions.
